moduleName: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud

questions.questionText: What is the primary objective of a Business Email Compromise (BEC) attack targeting remote finance workers?

options.text: To manipulate remote workers into transferring corporate funds or changing payment details to attacker-controlled accounts.
To send free software licenses to employees.

questions.explanation: BEC targets financial communications to divert payments to fraudulent accounts (Lazarus, 2024).

questions.questionText: An email requesting an urgent update to a vendor's bank account details should always be verified by calling a phone number from the original master contract.
questions.explanation: Out-of-band verification using known contract phone numbers prevents invoice manipulation fraud.

questions.questionText: A remote employee emails HR from john.smith-work@gmail.com asking to change their direct deposit bank account before Friday's payroll. What should HR do?

options.text: Update the direct deposit details immediately.
Require the employee to submit the request through the secure internal HR portal or verify the request via a direct phone/video call.
Email the employee's password to gmail.com.

questions.explanation: Direct deposit changes sent via personal email accounts are primary targets for payroll interception.

questions.questionText: Which of the following indicate that an invoice update request may be a BEC attempt? (Select TWO)

options.text: The invoice email comes from a domain with a slight typo (supplier-billing.co instead of supplier-billing.com).
The request insists that payment MUST be wired within 2 hours to prevent account closure.
The vendor's banking details match the historical records on file.
The request was submitted through your company's secure vendor portal.

questions.explanation: Typosquatted domains and extreme artificial time pressure are indicators of BEC fraud.

questions.questionText: Calling the phone number listed on a suspicious new invoice is a safe way to verify if the invoice's bank account changes are real.
questions.explanation: If the invoice is fake, the phone number on it leads directly to the scammer. Use trusted numbers from master contracts.

questions.questionText: What internal financial control requires two separate individuals to review and approve wire transfers above a designated threshold?
questions.explanation: Dual-custody ensures that a single manipulated employee cannot execute unauthorized transfers alone.

questions.questionText: A long-time vendor emails an invoice for $22,000. The invoice matches the expected amount, but a note says: "Our bank is undergoing an audit. Wire payment to our new overseas account." What is the safest response?

options.text: Wire the $22,000 to the overseas account to avoid late fees.
Hold the payment and contact the vendor's CFO/accounting lead using your established, verified phone directory.
Forward the email to 5 random contacts.

questions.explanation: Audit excuses for sudden overseas account changes are common BEC pretexts requiring verification.

questions.questionText: In an email header, what field shows the actual mail server that sent the message, helping reveal domain spoofing?
questions.explanation: Email headers reveal true server origins, exposing sender address spoofing.

questions.questionText: Business Email Compromise (BEC) attacks only use fake domains; they never involve real, compromised vendor email accounts.
questions.explanation: Attackers frequently compromise real vendor accounts (Vendor Email Compromise) to send fraudulent invoices from actual mailboxes.

questions.questionText: Why do BEC scammers target remote finance workers right before weekends or major holidays?

options.text: Internet speeds are faster on weekends.
Staff are rushing to finish tasks and are more likely to bypass verification steps under time pressure.
Banks are closed on weekends so money transfers are free.
Computers automatically turn off on holidays.

questions.explanation: Rushing before deadlines reduces vigilance, increasing the likelihood that security protocols will be skipped.
